issue.body: this is my approach to solving the issue I found in #2592

body: What version of eslint are you running?

based on how you have solved this problem in your PR, it tells me that `object-assign` module does a shallow copy and not a deep copy?
Because if it does a deep copy then this problem should not come up.
I am saying this based on how you have solved the problem as I still have to look at the code at runtime.
Gotcha, yeah `object-assign` is definitely a shallow copy.

@gyandeeps You are correct. `object-assign` is only shallow copy. I wouldn't, however, want to bring in a whole new dependency just for one line of code. mergeConfig actually can do deep copy, so I would just use that.
@ilyavolodin I agree. If we have a way to do a deep copy without including a new dependency then its awesome.

Do you guys mean something like:

``` js
util.mergeConfigs({}, require(filePath));
```

instead of:

``` js
clone(require(filePath));
```
I've updated my PR accordingly, it appears to solve the problem equally well :)

To be more specific

``` js
var newConfig = util.mergeConfigs({}, require(filePath));
```

But yes, mergeConfigs was created to do deep copy of config objects.
@ilyavolodin @gyandeeps have either of you confirmed that this is a bug?
I haven't tried it myself, but looking at the code, and knowing that @gyandeeps confirmed it last time, this sounds about right.
